runs.text: Sixteen babies, born in a tent. Haiti, two thousand and ten. An earthquake flattens Port-au-Prince. Israel flies in a field hospital. Before it packs up, it treats one thousand one hundred and two people, runs three hundred and fourteen surgeries, and delivers those sixteen babies. Japan, two thousand and eleven. After the tsunami, an Israeli clinic opens in Minamisanriku. Its first patient? The town's mayor. Florida, two thousand and twenty one. A tower collapses in Surfside. Israel's rescue unit flies in to search beside American teams. Turkey, two thousand and twenty three. A huge earthquake. Israeli teams pull nineteen people out of the rubble. In twenty sixteen, the World Health Organization rated Israel's field hospital the first team in the world at its top level. And the very first mission? Greece, one thousand nine hundred and fifty three. Israel was five years old. Many countries send rescue teams. Israel is one of them. Should every country keep a team like this? Tell me below. Remember Haiti?
